problem: The clause 'With interpolation it also spills toward bin 1' contradicts the chapter's own bin layout. The chapter defines bin 9 as 160° ≤ θ < 180°, so its centre is 170°; a sample at exactly 170° sits at the centre of bin 9 and would not spill into bin 1 under linear interpolation. The spill only happens if bins are centred on 0°, 20°, …, 160° (the original paper's convention), which the chapter does not use.
fix: Say: 'With interpolation a vote near the 0°/180° boundary (for example 175°) splits between bin 9 and bin 1, but at exactly 170° it lies at the centre of bin 9 and does not split. Do not wrap it in a no-interpolation question.'

problem: The example L2-normalizes a single cell histogram, so a student may conclude that HOG normalizes each cell on its own. The chapter itself says normalization is per block (four cells concatenated), so the example needs one line saying it is practising the norm step only.
fix: Add after the answer: 'In full HOG this 9-number cell histogram is not normalized alone; it is concatenated with the other three cells of its block into a 36-number vector, and that vector is L2-Hys normalized.'

problem: The bins are edge-aligned ((k−1)·20° ≤ θ < k·20°, so 0° is the lower edge of bin 1), while classic HOG implementations centre the bins on multiples of 20° (0°, 20°, …, 160°, with 0° and 180° sharing one bin). A student comparing with OpenCV or the original paper will see 0° land in a different bin.
fix: Add one sentence: 'Some implementations centre the bins at 0°, 20°, …, 160° instead; the arithmetic here uses edge-aligned bins, so follow the convention stated in the question.'
